In this task scope, we are going to add a new dynamic configuration in admin panel which we will list the countries that business signup is allowed. This list will be used in {{business-portal}} service to get countries for signup. So we will have the following scenarios: 

# The country is on the list and the invoice issuer exists for the country → Allow signup
# The country is on the list, but there is no invoice issuer for the country → Don’t allow signup
# The country is not on the list, but there is an invoice issuer for the country → Don’t allow signup



*For future*

With these changes, we are not going to be able to target specific companies to allow signup. Let’s say we want to be enabled in the new country, and before going to live fully, we want to run all tests and be sure that every piece works perfectly. If we have only a dynamic configuration then adding a country is not enough as everyone in that country can register. So we can’t target a specific group because we don’t have any identifier at that time. 

But we are going to make changes to the signup flow in the future so we will create business admin at the first step and in the next steps we can use {{business_admin_user_id}} as the identifier and target them. In this task scope, we are not going to do it, but needed to be mentioned here.

Unfortunately, the column {{created}} is not an index column, so if you run the delete query as it is, it will lock the transaction to the target table for a long time.

This is the suggestion:

Example:

{noformat}_min_id, _max_id = select min(id) as min_id, max(id) as max_id FROM taxify_delivery_eta.eta;
                                                                                            
_start_id = _min_id;                                                                        
                                                                                            
for until _max_id:                                                                          
                                                                                            
  _end_id = _start_id + 1000;                                                               
                                                                                            
  DELETE                                                                                    
  FROM taxify_delivery_eta.eta                                                              
  WHERE id >= _start_id AND id < _end_id                                                    
  AND created < TIMESTAMP('2023-07-28')                                                     
  AND type = 'SEARCH';                                                                      
                                                                                            
  sleep 3 seconds;                                                                          
                                                                                            
  _start_id = _end_id;                                                                      
{noformat}

This is just a pseudo code, so you can change it as you wish; however, the key point is as follows:

# Use {{PK}} index ( {{id}} ) to narrow down the search and delete.
# Give a minimum of 3 seconds between each deletion so that replicas won’t impact by many deletions in the master.

I have now had the chance to review the proposed amendment. 

By accepting this amendment Bolt will retain the right to be able to terminate the Special Terms immediately, however Bolt will be removing its right of clawing back and charging the customer for any costs incurred when trying to retrieve monies owed.

If Bolt need to retrieve monies owed, Bolt will have to bare this cost and will be unable to claim this from the customer. If you feel the Customer will not default on payment (for example: if they have an outstanding credit rating or Bolt has a previous commercial relationship with the Customer so you know they are good for the money) accepting this amendment is low risk, as Bolt retains the right to terminate the terms immediately. However, if the Customer fails to make payment this could result in Bolt having to bare the cost of retrieving outstanding sums due.

Essentially, the decision on whether to accept this rests with your team (cc. [~accountid:6126107624912a0069eedb8f] )and whether they are happy to proceed with the amendment taking the above into account.

Considering that data will be transferred to Leapsome, and Leapsome uses sub-processors outside of the EEA (and in the USA), this becomes a higher risk processing activity and +must+ be subject to a DPA negotiated and signed between the parties. *We would recommend that Leapsome provide us their referenced Data Processing Addendum to review. Therefore, since our user didn’t hit the car and no one at Bolt directly caused these damages we can’t be held liable or accountable. This is referred to sometimes as Force Majeure or an Act of God. 

For example, if there were a strong wind which pushed the scooter over or a random person walked passed and pushed the scooter over. How can we or our users be held accountable for the actions of the wind or a random third party? 

So unless the car owner can prove without doubt we or our user are the proximate cause of this damage we are not insured for it.

I think {{INTERVAL 14 DAY}} is still a big scan considering the record size.

{{INTERVAL 1 HOUR}} scan 71,298 rows in my test.

So, my suggestion is as follows:

{noformat}_interval_date = 7                                                                                 
_interval_hour = 1                                                                                 
                                                                                                                                                                                                      
_end_date = SELECT MIN(last_update) AS end_date                                                    
FROM `salt`                                                                                        
WHERE last_update <  DATE_SUB(NOW(), INTERVAL _interval_date DAY)                                  
;                                                                                                  
                                                                                                                                                                                                      
FOR until _end_date:                                                                               
                                                                                                   
  _start_date = SELECT MAX(last_update) AS start_date                                              
                FROM `salt`                                                                        
                WHERE last_update =  DATE_SUB(NOW(), INTERVAL _interval_date DAY);                 
                                                                                                   
  _intermediate_date = SELECT MAX(last_update) AS interval_date                                    
                       FROM `salt`                                                                 
                       WHERE last_update =  DATE_SUB(_interval_date, INTERVAL _interval_hour HOUR);
                                                                                                   
  _loop_count = SELECT count(*)                                                                    
                FROM `salt`                                                                        
                WHERE last_update < _start_date                                                    
                AND last_update >= _intermediate_date;                                             
                                                                                                   
  _limit = 1000                                                                                    
                                                                                                   
  FOR _loop_count / _limit:                                                                        
                                                                                                   
    DELETE                                                                                         
    from `salt`                                                                                    
    FROM `salt`                                                                                    
    WHERE last_update < _interval_date                                                             
    AND last_update >= _intermediate_date                                                          
    LIMIT _limit;                                                                                  
                                                                                                   
    Sleep 3 seconds;                                                                               
                                                                                                   
  if _interval_hour <= 23:                                                                         
     _interval_hour++;                                                                             
  else:                                                                                            
     _interval_hour = 1;                                                                           
     _interval_date++;                                                                             
{noformat}

This is an example of pseudo-code, so you can change it as you wish; however, the key point is as follows:

# Narrow down the TiKV scan by using INTERVAL 1 HOUR ( 71,298 ). This will reduce the coprocess time.
# Give idle seconds ( in this example, it is 3 seconds ) between each DELETION in order to reduce the workload for TiCDC.

According to the requirements, we have to arrange the zoom level when:

* The screen is opened for the first time
* The user selects a new location from confirm on the map bottom sheet search

For the latter requirement, on Android, when the user selects a new location from confirm on the map bottom sheet search, we do not have the new LOR and when we receive the new LOR we lose the state that indicates the user had a new search. Thus, we could not find implementing such a zoom behavior.

Therefore, we decided to keep the zoom logic as it is until we solve the issues mentioned above.

# _Regarding the document shared with us, I recommend that you open a ticket for the Risk and Safety Team to ensure alignment with them_. - I'll initiate this once we agree on an approach

# _From a reclassification point of view_



*a) Putting in place processes allowing the fleet to block its drivers who are in breach of T&Cs, after this has been flagged by Bolt to the fleet*



Currently, this isn't feasible. Removing a driver from a fleet involves a manual process through our support team.



*b) Blocking the entire fleet in case one of its drivers is in breach of T&Cs.*This approach seems excessive as it affects multiple drivers. We have explored an alternative:- Assume the risk for potentially criminal events and enforce a hard block on the driver, with an option for appeal.



* Create a fleet-focused strategy for moderate/low-risk events and recurrences based on safety scores following this process:1. Driver flagged by safety score triggers an email to the fleet with detailed occurrences/reports.


# Fleet responds through a questionnaire, indicating their intention to block the driver.
# If the fleet decides to keep the driver active, and there is a recurrence, access to the fleet owner portal is restricted until the driver is blocked. (this means they won’t be able to add new drivers/cars).

However, upon thorough discussion of this option, we have arrived at the conclusion that it could potentially be construed as a form of driver block enforcement. Such an approach might be perceived as ethically and legally questionable. In the event of legal proceedings, there is a possibility that we could be deemed responsible for imposing the block on the driver.

c) To sum up, the most favorable choice would be this one. We will develop a form to facilitate the appeal process and ensure that all appeals receive appropriate attention from the OPS team. Could the legal team draft the content for communication related to blocking, outlining the necessary provision(s) from our T&Cs to be referenced?

_3. Finally, regarding “Implementing a trigger for driver profile analysis”_

This profiling will be new in PT and was developed by us. Please keep in mind that this is a simple process in which we’ll look at the safety reports from the last 3 months, attribute them points (e.g. a minor event is -10%) and check which drivers are deducted enough points (they’d all have the same starting point - 100%) to be below a threshold if define (e.g. 20%). Thank you

All changes were accepted with these exceptions:

*Alteração ao ponto 5.1 – Não Aceite*

Não nos parece razoável que a BOLT pretenda que os termos e condições que define unilateralmente como aplicáveis, a operadores de táxi e a motoristas ao seu serviço, sejam livremente alteráveis por si e aplicáveis ao nosso contrato sem nosso acordo prévio, visto que tais alterações podem ter implicações para os nossos cooperadores e respectivos motoristas, pelo que não é aceitável tal discricionariedade.

Assim, sugerimos a seguinte redacção:

_"5.1.    Sem prejuízo das disposições particulares do presente Contrato, os Termos e Condições aplicáveis a Operadores de Táxi e a Motoristas ao seu serviço, disponíveis no website da BOLT, e que constituem anexo do presente contrato, são aplicáveis às relações contratuais estabelecidas entre a BOLT e os Operadores de Táxi e os motoristas ao serviço destes, registados na Plataforma BOLT, sendo certo que a alteração das mesmas para ser aplicável no domínio deste contrato carecerá de acordo entre as contratantes."_

No limite, se a BOLT não abrir mão do seu propósito de alterar unilateralmente tais condições, entendo que deveríamos estabelecer a faculdade de as alterações só nos serem aplicáveis após nos serem notificados e nos ser concedido o direito de fazer cessar de imediato o  contrato.



JR: Não vejo problema em notificá-los e dar-lhes o poder de cessar de imediato contrato caso discordem.  



*Alteração ao ponto 4.3 da nossa proposta – Não Aceite a total eliminação desta clausula*

Não concordamos com a eliminação integral da nossa proposta. Propomos uma nova redacção, a saber:

_"4.3.    Nesta fase, e para habilitar o PARCEIRO ao cumprimento do estabelecido em 4.2., a BOLT compromete-se a assegurar todos os seus esforços para que se concretize a  entrega semanal de, pelo menos, 10000 (dez mil) serviços ao PARCEIRO. sem que garanta o cumprimento de tal objectivo."_

JR: Parece-me que, com esta redação, não somos efetivamente obrigados a entregar por isso estou ok. Só alteraria para um valor por sócio e não total (creio que não será tema).

Hello [~accountid:5d723b3830f82c0c36be5b56] thank you for raising this ticket and for the great feedback.

_Driver is asking to add Comfort, but in admin, there is no tag for Comfort Category for his car._

As long as the Comfort category is available in the relevant country, all the applicable categories will be always visible for the agents to choose from. 

If the question is about why the drivers don’t have a Comfort category tag for their vehicle, it solely depends on the category criteria, which are defined by the Local OPS and are shared with agents in internal documents or, as you mentioned in the KB. 

The categories are publicly visible in KB only for the following countries: Czech Republic, Norway, Saudi Arabia, Poland, Germany, Finland, UK, France, and Portugal. 

*Actions on your feedback:*

h3. Driver wants to add a new category

*-Step 1: Review the driver’s request-*

-If the driver should fill in the form in order to register their vehicle in a new category:-

* -Advise the driver accordingly and provide them with the link-
* -If needed, approach the local OPS team to consult-

Explanation: This part doesn't make much sense, as drivers don't have to proceed with any source of category registration. The vehicles have the categories added manually. So, if a driver wants to change it because they believe they are eligible for an additional one(s), they need to raise a CS ticket.

*Suggested edit, first part (Step 1: Review the driver’s request)*

* *_Check if the vehicle meets the requested category requirements in the market category articles in KB. If your market doesn't have vehicle categories publicly visible, request the vehicle category requirements from your local OPS_*
* Review the photos of the vehicles provided (if any)
* If needed, approach the local OPS team to consult
* If the vehicle doesn’t qualify for the requested category, advise the driver accordingly
* If the vehicle meets the requirements, continue to step 2

*Suggested edit, second part (Driver asks how to change categories in the app)*

h3. Driver asks how to change categories in the app

Advise the driver that they can choose categories for which they are currently getting orders in the app:

* After they go online, they can select categories by clicking on the vehicle icon on the right side of the screen
* They can change the categories whenever they are online.
* *_If the driver is unsure of which categories they are eligible for, provide them with the list of categories they can apply for._*

*Note:* The instructions are also available in the FAQ article [How to select ride category in the app|https://beehive.bolt.eu/main/kb/articles/public/115002931533].



Feel free to add any additional info you would consider important.

Have a great weekend!

David

AWS Lake Formation provides fine-grained permission management for the AWS Glue Data Catalog. Traditionally, access to AWS Glue Data Catalog is controlled by AWS IAM. Lake Formation uses tag-based access control to allow more fine grained AWS Glue access.

[AWS Athena, Glue, Redshift and EMR support Lake Formation. |https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lake-formation/latest/dg/working-with-services.html]There are third-party tools which allow other [query engines|https://aws.amazon.com/lake-formation/faqs/] to integrate with Lake Formation, one of them is Privacera which allows to integrate Databricks with Lake Formation. However, none of these solutions are neither freely available nor open source, so we would have to write our own solution.

There is a short documentation on how to [integrate with Lake Formation|https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lake-formation/latest/dg/Integrating-with-LakeFormation.html]. Based on these docs, I imagine a custom solution would be a Spark [ExternalCatalogListener|https://github.com/apache/spark/blob/master/sql/catalyst/src/main/scala/org/apache/spark/sql/catalyst/catalog/ExternalCatalogWithListener.scala], which would be provided as a jar to databricks clusters. This plugin would intercept calls to AWS Glue Data Catalog and instead call Lake Formation API. Lake Formation provides temporary credentials (AWS STS) to registered AWS S3 locations, so that Spark can read the data.

As mentioned, Lake Formation uses tags for access control. What could our source of tags be, so that our custom ExternalCatalogListener can read and include them in Lake Formation API calls?

It seems possible to write a custom integration for Databricks Spark with Lake Formation, however, this sounds like a massive engineering effort.

Also note that the adjusted field actually is not a boolean, but an indicator of the model used: [https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGINEERING/pages/3830351408/Dedicated+Courier+ETA+model+documentation|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGINEERING/pages/3830351408/Dedicated+Courier+ETA+model+documentation|smart-link] . Hey!

I agree with you on that. It looks contradictory indeed.

Our biggest wish is to accept the item from driver only when we know who the owner is. This way we can contact the owner and organise the return for the item. 

It’s also okay to accept the item if we do not know who the owner is, but only in cases when the item costs less than 50 euros. In this case we’re free to utilise it after 30 days. Items that cost more than 50 euros and can not be related to their owner - should be provided by drivers straight to the nearest police station. If they provide them to us, it’s an additional task for us, to submit a report to police and to bring the items to police ourselves.

Why all these ‘'complications’'? - Only because of past experience. From previous years we had truly a lot of items left in the office, they were only piling up.

With approach that’s described in this message, drivers seem to be more disciplined and really check at the end of each ride if there is anything left in the car. Because they do acknowledge that if they find an item in car that costs over 50 euros, they will have to use their time to report it to police themselves.

I do hope that it all makes sense. Please, let me know if you feel like this all is rather confusing and you’d suggest to stay with the version that we started this ticket with.

Hey [~accountid:618d20acfba4d0006ae30dd3] 

Principally this is a valid use case, and indeed quite recently we looked into it in Estonia as an insurance company wanted to make use of Bolt Drive for similar reasons. _Though anecdotal evidence shows vast majority of our Business customer users are Customer employees there are also its subcontractors, clients, etc. We don’t limit this as long as it’s in Business Customers commercial and/or professional capacity._

However it’s 3.2 and 6.4 of Business General T&C which are problematic for such Business customers - for somewhat understandable reasons they’d prefer not to take up such broad liability for any ancillary cost (fines, damage claims, etc) caused by users with whom they don’t have such close connection as one might have with an employee.

Principally we could make a business decision to waive Business customers liability for such ancillary cost, and rely solely on charging it from the user, but there 2 blockers atm:
1. There doesn’t seem to be technical/operational clarity internally on the product level from whom we are capable of charging this operationally (I [investigated it personally recently and even the information I did manage to gather|https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1pTrEXMitBLlTZVAzoQXFddr2hEl9ypoCUDvJTSHQdGI/edit#gid=1502425558] was somewhat controversial from Product and Ops) - until this is cleared I strongly advise not to waive the liability of the Business customer, but rather explore the option described by Elina, i.e. for the Business customer to sort it out with its users itself. Meanwhile feel free to escalate this to Business Product (via your reporting line or directly) as otherwise this will never get prioritized.

2. The Drive T&C’s are not clear enough to confidently enforce charges on users for services used under Business payment method. This is on me to suggest relevant changes to the T&C’s + implementation time. Scheduled for Aug-Sept.

Happy wknd!

For purposes of audit trail, see below a recap of discussion from slack:

Advised we need an agreement which contains appropriate C-P provisions in the agreement. [~accountid:61b0698dfe9f3000680f0585] has updated the template you shared to incorporate appropriate C-P provisions - [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1C66Lj_3KCz4Nt6gPhM9ikyWbBMbl78TPtGrSkSILNZg/edit?pli=1|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1C66Lj_3KCz4Nt6gPhM9ikyWbBMbl78TPtGrSkSILNZg/edit?pli=1|smart-link] . This version should be shared with DLA for discussion/alignment.  

Some additional actions the Privacy Legal Team will need to take: 

* *Legal Basis* - As we’ve now identified this is ‘personal data’, we’ll need to complete a Legitimate Interest Assessment to document which legal basis we’re relying on for the transfer of the data.
* *Privacy Notice* - As currently drafted the Driver Privacy Notice does not cover sharing with targets / their advisers as part of M&A transactions. We’d already identified this as a deficiency in the current notice and are in the process of updating. This is a known risk which will not be addressed before the data is shared but will be addressed in coming months.

Hi [~accountid:6151cf6878e5e40070fb74c2] 

please find below my comments for FR: 

* *Enforceability - acceptance flow* 

Users must have had access these terms before they use the services and must have expressly accepted it. Otherwise, these terms will not be enforceable against them. As highlighted in the [separate ticket |https://taxify.atlassian.net/browse/LSS-20179]on this topic, to mitigate the risk that the clause would be considered unenforceable we should add the Marketplace Guidelines as an Annex to the T&Cs going through the acceptance flow. 

* *Blocking mechanism*

The breach of the rules set out in the Marketplace Conduct Guidelines triggers the bad rider blocking feature. However, according to FR case law and consumer law, any contractual clause granting the business platform  discretionary power to delete or terminate users' accounts, whenever they contravene the "Rules" issued by the company relating to the type of content and behavior authorized without it being foreseen or justification or notice:

* *is unfair insofar it creates a significant imbalance for the benefit of the professional and to the detriment of the consumer*
* *is presumed to be unfair and the presumption is not rebuttable as the professional has full discretion in determining whether or not the consumer’s behaviour complies with the contractual provisions.*

The Unfair Terms Commission recommends inserting a notice period and specific and sufficiently serious grounds for suspension to justify the suspension, failing which the clause will be irrefutably presumed to be unfair, in that it leaves the professional the right to determine discretionary the reasons that could lead to the suspension.

Several companies have been condemned on the basis of abusive clauses (Article L212-1 of the Consumer Code) for having inserted this type of clause in their general conditions, in particular Twitter, in 2018 by the Paris TGI.

*To minimize the risk that the clause termination of the contract and the services will be considered abusive by the French courts, our recommendations are as follows:*

* +*prior warnings and notice period:*+ provide an initial warning to the Passenger before the suspension of their access to the app, then, if the breaches persist, inform the Passenger before the suspension of access to the app , respecting a reasonable notice period and writing.
* +*spell out situations/ breaches that lead to blocking*+ +:+ breaches that may lead to suspension must be s*pecifically targeted and be serious enough to justify* the suspension of access to the service. Only breaches of legal obligations ( such as criminal law infringements eg theft, violence, harassment, discrimination, etc.) or serious contractual breaches (non-payment for the service) can justify the termination of the service. 
* +*right of appeal :*+ the Passenger must be able to contest the suspension decision and be compensated in the event of an unjustified / fraudulent suspension.

For all the other samples (that have {{_track_}} in name) it seems to be user login funnel analytics.



Some of the events have {{userId: "client-130068971"}} and {{properties.user_id: 174199179}} 

Why is the number from {{userId}} and {{user_id}} different? (it should refer to the same user)

* userId is send by mobile app as distinct_id - and we put it in the event without checking it
* user_id is computed by us in the backend based on request.phone_number ({{SELECT id FROM user WHERE phone = request.phone}})

Still, why they are different?

User with id {{130068971}} is logged in on multiple devices (one of the is {{D1}}) - disctinct_id is {{client-130068971}} after login

User with id {{130068971}} is archived (CHECKED IN DB FOR SAMPLES) - but {{D1}} doesn’t know about archival

User opens app on {{D1}} and mobile app calls {{appState/get/v1}} and sends {{distinct_id: client-130068971}}

Backend returns {{login_state: null}} (because user was archived)



Mobile app doesn’t refresh distinct_id on  {{login_state: null}} , so distinct id will stay the same {{client-130068971}}, being linked to the previous account (which is archived). That is why events are being sent for suppressed account.

h3. {color:#36b37e}*Summary of changes in the process*{color}

[Updated process model in Figma|https://www.figma.com/file/bTrCcKPOXSz2JILZHTY96N/%F0%9F%9A%97-Rider-paid-cash-for-in-app-payment?type=whiteboard&node-id=170-476&t=ogm4FYDhoHYf4BuQ-0]

*Market-specific steps*

* +_🇺🇦 Ukraine - if there is no history of rides/successful payments - no refund._+ This step is *not removed* because it is reducing fraud in the market and that was working well so far, so removal could lead to fraud increase. However, this step could be replaced by the “Refund abuse prevention feature” when it goes live.
* +_🇦🇿 Azerbaijan - if the trip took place within the last month - full refund, if the trip is older than 1 month - no refund._+ This step is *not removed* but moved from the compensation part to confirm the circumstances. The market has the highest incoming volumes compared to other markets (5,237 in the last 3 months) and they receive a lot of false claims from riders. The reason for the 1-month time limit is to prevent situations where riders make an order, forget about it, and then later (after they see a negative Bolt balance mostly) submit false claims about paying in cash. However, this step could be replaced by the “Refund abuse prevention feature” when it goes live.
* +_🇬🇧 UK - if the driver was asking for money to cover a toll fee/congestion charge, the case is not safety-related._+ This note is *changed to Global*. The safety team explained that the reason why drivers ask for cash when it comes to toll fees/airport fees/congestion charges is simply because they don't have cash on them at that moment in time to pay the fare. This does not mean the driver is being untruthful in any way or fraudulent. This note will reduce unnecessary escalations to Safety (reducing the HT, TRT, and avoiding back and forth).
* +_🇮🇪 Ireland - check if the price is 0EUR in Admin, confirm with the driver how much cash he took, and calculate and deduct the commission fee._+ These instructions are *changed to Global*. If a driver submits a PR and notes that the trip was paid in cash, CS should close the PR at 0 EUR to avoid overcharging the rider. This approach is likely already followed globally to prevent double charging, even if initially it was meant only for Ireland. This action is logical, as confirming the full price would later require a refund to the rider. Another reason why we need this step globally is to prevent drivers from having orders without paying the commission fee. This could help decrease such situations where drivers realize they can't avoid the fee by taking cash.
* +_🇵🇹 Portugal - no refund to the rider. Promo code based on the severity._+ This step *is removed*, and the market will follow global steps. 
* +_🇦🇿 Azerbaijan and 🇺🇦 Ukraine - do not compensate the rider if it is not the 1st time._+ This step *is removed*, and markets will follow global steps.
* +_🇫🇷 France - market-specific Slack workflow for driver quality._+ Instructions *are removed* as they are no longer followed. The market will create an SD ticket with all the articles that had these instructions and we will also remove them. 

*Compensation part*

* +_Automation does not exist_+ - there is nothing in the [Current Support Automations 🤖|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CD/pages/4294410600/Current+Support+Automations] list, also test ticket did not trigger any automation. Decisions related to automation are removed from the updated process model.
* +_Ignoring the payment_+ - this action will be taken always if the payment was failed because it is impossible for CS to make the rider update their payment method and pay one more time for the ride that they paid in cash.
* +_Compensation decision_+ - before compensating CS will consider only if it is the 1st time. At first it made sense to also consider who is at fault (rider or driver), however, even if the rider incorrectly selected the payment method and it looks like the rider’s fault, the driver can always see the payment method in his app, so he should check that before taking cash from the rider. It makes the driver to be always at fault, because it is his responsibility to check if he actually has to take cash, before taking it.
** 1st time - full refund to BB (actor: Driver)
** Not the 1st time - no comp or small comp to BB/promo code.

*Removed steps*

* +_Confirming the circumstances_+ - the first step in the process was to find out who is the cash payment initiator, but this information didn’t change the course of the following actions. The step is removed because it doesn't lead anywhere. The refund is based on the history of previous reports and the education about selecting the correct payment method should be done in any case. Finding out who is at fault is not realistic, as rider & driver most probably will have different sides of the story, and clarifying this information might increase AHT.
* +_Log the report_+ - removed as in Beehive it is done automatically and we don’t use Zendesk anymore.
* +_Leave a comment_+ - the step was duplicated, thus one was removed.
* +_Rider education_+ - the part to educate the rider that the driver can consider additional cash as a tip was removed. This sentence might trigger the rider and affect the CSAT because the rider reports this as an issue to CS and we shouldn’t try to justify the situation supporting the driver.
* +_Markets where BQS is not live_+ - market names and flags were removed to avoid confusion because France has their own market-specific instructions, also Spain will have them too soon, so having the flags might cause confusion on whether both instructions need to be followed. Markets without BQS and without market-specific steps should understand that these instructions are for them, without adding their flag.

*Optimized steps*

* +_Safety_+ - guidelines on what to do if the case is Safety-related were too far in the process, thus they are now moved to the first decision, in order to avoid unnecessarily following the process.

Hey [~accountid:5cfe57d9a7095c0c3ffac38d], I have mapped the first part of the vehicle adjustment process. It’s a well-written article, but I would suggest making a couple of changes and as discussed, *checking countries with high AHT.*  

The article is[ HERE|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360005187534].

# *„Declined silently“ rejection reason is not clear.*

*Context*: Globally, the main reason for declined silently applications are *duplicates.* The local OPS team is usually not making comments on such car applications, so the only viable option now is escalation without proper investigation, at least according to the current article. I believe if we explain better to CS how to recognize duplicates, we can improve the KPIs.

*The fix* suggestion is in this comment: [https://www.figma.com/file/RxDLCRKBxRI8BceJpsX7lf?node-id=34:1380#516944332|https://www.figma.com/file/RxDLCRKBxRI8BceJpsX7lf?node-id=34:1380#516944332|smart-link] 



*2. Driver verification process for linking vehicle requests from invalid emails.* 

Context: I want to confirm if we’re sure that we can or we should attend to the requests from invalid emails at all. As an example, if a driver requests any change of their profile, the CS is advising them to contact us from a valid email address or in-app. My concern is, why the flow is different for managing the vehicles. 

*Next step:* Clear out if we should attend to requests from different email addresses at all. Instead, we can consider advising the driver how to change their email address.

*Additional note:* This can be a reason for high AHT if the CS is requesting ID checks. 

*Relevant comment on the map*: [https://www.figma.com/file/RxDLCRKBxRI8BceJpsX7lf?node-id=0:1#519299198|https://www.figma.com/file/RxDLCRKBxRI8BceJpsX7lf?node-id=0:1#519299198|smart-link] 



3. The article should be split to *add*/*remove*/and *link* to existing vehicles.

Relevant comment: [https://www.figma.com/file/RxDLCRKBxRI8BceJpsX7lf?node-id=7:208#515694010|https://www.figma.com/file/RxDLCRKBxRI8BceJpsX7lf?node-id=7:208#515694010|smart-link] 

*Note:* While the article title says „change“, changing vehicle details is not covered in this article, and is misleading. The dedicated article already exists[ here|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360019169760].

4. We should inform all the drivers about the local doc requirement.

In [the relevant article|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360005187534], we are randomly saying that agents should inform the driver about the doc requirements only for Tanzania, and it seems very much out of place. Instead, we should aim to streamline the process and teach agents to inform the drivers about the local requirements automatically.



Please let me know what you think. Also, any feedback on this summary format is appreciated.

Following discussions with Florian, we reached the conclusion that the best course of action is probably to do (almost) nothing.

The problem is as follows:

For batched orders (around 15% of normal orders, around 40% of Bolt Market orders iirc), a courier queue is created with more than one order. This courier queue shows the order in which the courier needs to perform the pick-up and drop-off actions for the assigned orders. Now, if the courier or any call to moveState attempts to perform a pick-up or drop-off action that is not next in the queue, an inconsistent queue error occurs.

When we time out a batched order or when CS manually succeeds an order, the order tries to go through all states until the final state is reached. The issue is that it might attempt a state change which is not next in the courier queue. For queues with 2+ orders, the orders are usually interleaved because the courier needs to pick up all of them before starting any drop-offs. This is why we constantly encounter this error. However, if you play a little game of ping pong and try to time out the first order, then the second one, and then the first one again, both should be successfully timed out. This is because, even with the inconsistent queue error, the order's states are changed to that point before the error.

Let's discuss possible solutions:

# When an order is batched, we time out or manually succeed the entire batch, even if we only sent the call to succeed one order. The difficulty here is detecting when it's a manual/timeout call (probably a special flag in moveState). Additionally, we lose the ability to manually act on just one order (who knows in what strange state the courier could be, where CS needs to succeed only one order in the batch to unblock them).
# When an order is batched, and we time out or manually succeed it, we ignore all the courier queue consistency checks and move it to the final state. Here, we need the flag, again, to recognize that it needs to pass through the consistency checks like a knife through butter. Moreover, and this is crucial, we need to ensure that the courier queue remains consistent by removing the relevant action from the queue. This solution is riskier because we could introduce serious bugs with the queue, resulting in the couriers being unable to change their order states.

However, as I mentioned at the beginning, both Florian and I don't believe that these quite significant changes are worth it for an error that is not necessarily a bug. It's also an error that can be ignored:

# For timeouts, from what I've seen, they still time out after a little ping pong game. The issue there lies with the errors, but we could handle the error in the timeout service and only log it as a notice.
# For manually succeeding orders, we could add a warning message in the admin panel form, but only when it's a batched order, so that CS/OPS knows that they might need to play a ping pong game with the batched orders.

h2. Analysis of DSAT cases

* CS insists on the description of the item even though it should be already quite clear (e.g. [house keys|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/224018167]). We should still ask for that but contact the driver even if we don’t know the color of something (e.g. [here|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/224890768] agent asked for a description 3 times before they started handling the case, it took 5 days to find out the color and shape of glasses ‼️)
* CS tells the rider that the driver will contact them but doesn’t mention if the driver has or doesn’t have an item (example [1|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/224018167], [2|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/224388904]).
* According to the current process, CS first asks about the description of the item only then for the consent > consent can be asked immediately in the first message ([example|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/224388904]).
* Sometimes drivers don’t call riders even though they promised to do, I suspect it’s not an infrequent scenario, so we may need to cover it (example [1|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/224388904], [2|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/224018167]).
* CS telling riders that we are not responsible for lost items doesn’t bring any value for the user (it’s actually already removed from the process). 
* In most cases I reviewed, if it was less than 24 hrs, riders tried to contact the driver but the driver wasn’t picking up.
* Agents can see which articles a user viewed so if they viewed the self-help article for lost items, then there’s really no point in asking them to contact the driver. There’s no point in asking them to contact the driver even if they didn’t view the article since they already contacted us.



*Follow-up actions:*

* Change the order of this [step|https://www.figma.com/file/hNh1FDu4jwmeOxQat7SZJi?node-id=521:1016#520493113] (/) 
* Add a new scenario [here|https://www.figma.com/file/hNh1FDu4jwmeOxQat7SZJi?node-id=521:2698#520496788] and that CS should tell R if D has their item or not (/) 
* Emphasize that CS shouldn’t request a very precise description of the lost item (e.g. a description of keys) [here|https://www.figma.com/file/hNh1FDu4jwmeOxQat7SZJi/Rider-lost-an-item?type=whiteboard&node-id=521-1017&t=iEl1YzbsIot9V8gM-4] (/)

[~accountid:712020:0b1ccfcb-3809-460a-88ab-c96985ba329a] my yesterday evening mind map on this:


**

# *Introduction:* The employer can control the fulfillment of work obligations, but the basic rights of the employee must be respected. Such processing of personal data can take place under specific circumstances on the basis of the legitimate interest of an employer.The employer must therefore start with a thorough analysis of the assessment and weighing of interests, from which it must be clear how the employer's interests outweigh the employee's right to privacy, and if this is proven, how the employer can control the employee in such a way that it infringes on the employee's privacy as little as possible.
----
# *Question:* Can we use the information from the access management system to give the direct supervisor accurate information about which days employees visit the office?
----
# *Remarks:*
## *Requirement for employees to work on premise:* A review of my personal employment contract reveals that the contract limits the work location to Tallinn and does not clearly specify that a specific office is my main work location. In principle, however, one can assume that the place of work is the dedicated office and that, as long as no general specifications have been made, the office is the place where the work is to be performed. Such a specification can be found for example in confluence where it is stated that the employer expects everybody to work from the office and in most roles, the minimum is 2-3 days of the time on site (hybrid). Remote work should be aligned with the manager.*Bolt expects employees to work 2-3 days per week in the office. The days are to be clarified with the manager. Here it would have to be clarified under labor law how legally binding the requirement for office use is (2-3 working days in the office).* 

## *Legal Basis for processing:* If no direct monitoring and recording obligation is prescribed by law, a legitimate interest of the employer may arise due to welfare and monitoring obligations, whereby the data protection interests of the employees must be taken into account here (see AKI recommendation: Employee monitoring).Processing is necessary for the purposes of the legitimate interests of the controller or of a third party, except where such interests are overridden by the interests or fundamental rights and freedoms of the data subject which require the protection of personal data
* *Necessity:* A processing activity is necessary if no milder means of achieving the purpose can be considered or if milder means are not equally suitable for achieving the purpose. 
*Example:* _Several variants can be considered for a report on office use:_  
_VAR 1 - Markus was in the office on Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday in calendar week 32_
_OR_ 
_Var 2 - Markus was in the office on 3 of 5 days in calendar week 32_
_OR_ 
_VAR 3 - Markus was in the office at least to the prescribed extent in calendar week 32_
* *Proportionality*
The processing activity would have to be proportionate with regard to the purpose it pursues.
- *legitimate purpose:* Verification that employees are in the office 2-3 times as required _(The request indicates that the purpose is "performance management". It should at least be made clear how the work in the office affects performance.)_
- *legitimate means:*Currently, it is still unclear to me how this message should be implemented. However, it should be implemented in such a way that the chosen reporting tool serves the purpose and is at the same time the mildest intervention (no more information than necessary, access only for the necessary group of recipients).
*  *Suitability:* Is the data from the access management system suitable as a record of office attendance?
----
*4. System:* Bolt does not use a timekeeping system. Rather, the access management system is to be used, whose primary function is a security measure of the building and not an employee-oriented time and location recording . It is not yet known in which form data from the system will be made available to the managers, but it is currently stated that the access will be via the Excel list used by the facility management. It is strongly recommended to define the access rights in advance to ensure that only authorized persons (e.g. supervisors) have access to employee-related data (it should be urgently avoided that, for example, managers from the marketing team have information about the office presence of legal team members).
----
*5. Transparency and data subject rights:* Bolt should tell people in advance about the oversight tools we’re using. They should understand what you’re doing and what’s expected of them. Neither the employment contract (I checked mine) nor from the privacy notice for employees this data processing is mentioned in a clear and understandable form and we would have to adapt the notice (probably also on the Confluence page which specifies the hybrid model, but this is not a data protection issue).

Hi [~accountid:6164570ec7bea4006994fde7], 

The assessment of when and how drivers should be blocked is generally to be done by local ops and the safety team and not by legal. If the team made the assessment that the driver should be blocked based on the events that occurred then the threat to sue us should not affect such assessment. However, please be aware that it should be clear from the communication to the driver why he was blocked and for how long. 

Please discuss this further with the local team to determine if you want to unblock this driver, the threat to sue us should not be such a reason unless the driver has not behaved badly and the block was unreasonable from our side to begin with. 

From a legal perspective it is important that we only block drivers when it is necessary based on the guidelines provided by the safety team. When drivers are blocked it is important that we maintain a good dialogue with them and seek to understand what has actually happened. However, a threat to sue us based on being blocked due to a safety incident is not reason enough to simply unblock the driver. 

This is not a legal matter in itself and should be solved with local ops and safety team. Hence, I will close this ticket but please raise a new ticket if you need legal support. 

Best regards, 

Michelle

Hi, from employment law side:

# There is an obligation to specify the place of work in the employment contract (Article 5 (1) 8. of Estonian Employment Contracts Act.). In addition Article 20 of the same act states that an employee must perform their duties +at the employer’s place of business+ which has the strongest connection with the employment relationship, unless the place of performance of work has been agreed on. It is presumed that the place of performance of work is agreed upon with the precision of the local government. This is also regulated in the BOLT TECHNOLOGY OÜ AND BOLT OPERATIONS OÜ RULES OF WORK ORGANISATION where clause 4.2.2. states that unless otherwise provided by applicable law or employment contract, an Employee shall do the work in the agreed place. So for the conclusion - +there is a legal obligation for employee to work at the agreed place of work which in case of Tallinn should be Bolt offices in Tallinn.+ 
# Employment Law’s usually don’t provide specific control mechanisms for the employer rather than just states that employer can issue disciplinary measures or terminate employment contract in case of violation of employment contract or internal rules by the employee. +Employer can implement specific control mechanisms taking into account relevant legal regulation in each country+. Planned use of access management system might not be the proper way how to monitor this as it can be unreliable and can be bypassed - using someone else’s card, coming in with somebody else etc.

First of all, I want to let you know that a Delivery Risk Review is ongoing and the most up-to-date safety SOPs will be published in the KB by the end of the month 🤞.  

----

* _What time frame should have passed before the contact from the eater in terms of_ [_food poisoning_|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/4417977090962] _for agents to actually believe the eaters' claim? Quite often we receive reports an hour after the delivery._ 

I am no expert here, but I checked online and it really depends:

_The symptoms of food poisoning usually begin within 1 to 2 days of eating contaminated food. They can also start a few hours later or several weeks later._

Besides this, the main idea is that all reports should be investigated. We should not assume a report to be malicious.

----

* _If courier reports that the front bumper of his car was_ [_damaged in an incident_|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/4505791026066]_, can we consider it as HP? Or does it depend on the severity of the issue with the bumper? For example, if it is slightly “bruised“ (for the lack of better word_ 😁_), then it is not an HP? But if it is entirely lost, then it is?_ 

Yes, it is safety in case of *Courier in Vehicle Accident Causing Injury or Structural Damage*. If there is no structural damage, but it’s only cosmetic, then no need. 

----

* _If the eater reports or during a callback agents notice that the voice of the speaker is female, but the app states that the courier should be male, is it enough evidence to consider_ [_account sharing_|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/4505534209810] _and treat as HP?_

Good point. I would say yes and I will add it to the SOP. 

----

* If a deaf courier is driving with a child who is acting as a “translator“ for the disabled courier, can we consider it as[ not alone in the vehicle|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/4505592050066] and treat as HP?
* Identically, if an Ukrainian courier is driving with a child who helps them to translate and communicate in English, is it an [HP|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/4505592050066]? 

I will check with my team and let you know asap. Here it’s mainly a privacy concern. 

----

* Can we treat a mold report in food identically to[ expired products|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/4418257894546] and look at it as HP case? Since there is no expiration date issue, just a quality report, agent was rather confused how to proceed in this particular [ticket|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/case/136519953].

Mold doesn’t necessarily mean the product is expired, so we would have the wrong date. But I understand the concern here and I will bring it up with the team. I’ll let you know asap.

----

# Can [dents and scratches|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/4505791026066] on the car or a bike can be considered as a HP? Please look at the attached image. 

No, it would not be considered safety. The vehicle condition is up to the courier. What’s the context of this picture though?

*copy of the mail*

“Dear Yuliia,
You can find our response to the raised question on the compliance of the current payment model of Bolt upon the adoption of the Draft Law on Road Transportation. Following points should be considered:
* *_From the perspective of legislation on currency regulation:_*
Kindly be informed that the ride-hailing operator activities proposed by the Draft Law refers to the establishment of service communication between the taxi drivers and customers/passengers. Since the ride-hailing operator (in your case, it is assumed to be already existing local entity Bolt Services AZ) will provide the ride-hailing services to both categories, the income should be transferred directly to the operator’s bank account instead of being transferred to Bolt OY’s bank account located outside the borders of the Republic of Azerbaijan. Legal basis for this limitation is affiliated with the requirements stipulated under the [“Rules for transactions of residents of the Republic of Azerbaijan in foreign currency, as well as of non-residents in national and foreign currency”|https://e-qanun.az/framework/34248] dated 28 November 2016 (hereinafter will be referred to as the ”Rules”).  Article 4.3 of the Rules regulates the types of operations based on which the transfers in foreign currency are carried out from the Republic of Azerbaijan to bank accounts located abroad. According to Article 4.3.1.2 of the Rules, one of the grounds allowing such transfer is the payment by residents and non-residents for the services imported to the Republic of Azerbaijan. As per the definition given in the Rules - imported services are +services and works performed by non-residents in the territory of the Republic of Azerbaijan+, as well as +services and works performed outside the country for the benefit of residents and non-residents+. It is worth noting that only the ground of payment for the imported services is related to the activities of Bolt company among all other operation types defined by the referred Article 4.3. However, considering that with the proposed changes, Bolt OY will not be registered as the ride-hailing operator and provide services in the Republic of Azerbaijan, this ground will not be applicable for the possibility of transfers. Thus, effective legislation for the currency legislation does not provide any legal basis in order to maintain Bolt company’s current payment model upon the Draft Law.
* *_From the perspective of personal data protection requirements:_*
Second point is related to the requirements on the storage and transfer of the personal data stipulated under the Law on Personal Data. Up until now, in practice of the ride-hailing services in the Republic of Azerbaijan, compliance with the data protection requirements has not been subject to strict government control which allowed the transfer and storage of personal data of the customers as well as the taxi drivers abroad. On the other side, upcoming reforms aims at addressing this issue by determining a direct obligation and corresponding liability for the ride-hailing operators on the protection of personal data as well as state registry of information systems and timely transfer of certain information to the respective executive authority. Current payment model of Bolt already includes the storage of the personal data (personal information, bank account details, etc.) of the customers abroad and within the non-registered information which is not compliant with the requirements of personal data rules.
*_Proposed model of implementation:_*
In order to transfer the income to the foreign accounts,  BOLT OY can establish a branch in the Republic of Azerbaijan in order to be able to use the current payment model. The new amendments to the Road Transportation Law indicates that the legal entities and sole trades can apply to the permission to act as an operator. However Article 1.0.4 of the Law on Licenses and Permits (the specific and primary law in licence and permission related matters in Azerbaijan) enlarges the scope of applicants and includes the legal entity (refers to entities established in the Republic of Azerbaijan), branch, representative office of a foreign legal entity and individual entrepreneur to this category. As the branch will act as an extension of the company’s business coverage and is established with the purpose of distribution of goods and services to a different location, they are considered to be a single unit for running business purposes.
 
In addition, the Law on Currency Regulations (as well as the Rules) classify the foreign legal entities, as well as their branches in Azerbaijan as «non-residents». Due to this statutory rule and single unit approach (applicable to the foreign legal entity and its branch), we may conclude that the payment for the services provided by the branches of foreign entities as the ride hailing operator (i.e. “imported services”) can be transferred to the foreign accounts of the head office. In addition to maintain all statutory requirements, BOLT should also register its information system in a local level and comply with the restrictions imposed to transfer of personal data. However, this suggested arrangement should be discussed with the Ministry of Digital Development and Transport as well as the Azerbaijan Ground Transport Agency (AYNA) before its implementation.
 
Should you need further clarification, please do not hesitate to contact us.
 
Best regards,
Shahlar”

Hey. The speed measuring device is not officially calibrated, we do not have any official paperwork to prove the accuracy.

The speedometer works by counting revolutions of the wheel (there are 30 magnets and 3 offset sensors that read the magnets inside the motor, which in total generate 90 pulses per motor revolution or one pulse per every 4 degrees, so it is very precise) and calculating scooter moving velocity through the motor rpm and the outer diameter of the tire.

A recommendation is to narrow down the Index scan:

AS-IS:

{noformat}SELECT                                          
 `unix_timestamp` (`created`) AS `created`,     
 `order_id`,                                    
 `device_uid`,                                  
 `city_id`,                                     
 `token`                                        
FROM                                            
 `order_device_live_activity`                   
WHERE                                           
`next_update_at` <= from_unixtime(1691564218)
LIMIT                                           
50;                                               
{noformat}

Recommendation:

{noformat}SELECT                                           
 `unix_timestamp` (`created`) AS `created`,      
 `order_id`,                                     
 `device_uid`,                                   
 `city_id`,                                      
 `token`                                         
FROM                                             
 `order_device_live_activity`                    
WHERE                                            
`next_update_at` <= from_unixtime(1691564218)    
and `next_update_at` > from_unixtime(1691567999)
LIMIT                                            
50;                                               
{noformat}

However, I would like to note a few concerns from a reclass point of view:

* as discussed earlier in the year, where we need to address drivers directly (e.g. for campaigns), it should be in a manner that indicates that the driver is “acting as representative of / on behalf of / at the service of” the fleet operator. This campaign, on the contrary, seems to be addressed directly to drivers and fleets are not at all part of it.
* bonus should ideally go to the fleet, not to the drivers, or we should say that Bolt is running a campaign which should allows drivers to increase earnings with the fleet (this second option not being as mitigating as the first one). Here this is not the case as well.  
* It is a major risk if anything is implemented directly between Bolt and drivers, as it seems to be the case of this campaign. Therefore, if the comercial decision is to still go ahead with the campaign, I would recommend to (a) further discuss the payment of the prizes to see if it follows the standard in place for all campaigns (b) consider involving fleet by identifying the winners as driver at the service of a given fleet, for instance.

h2. Main changes in the new process

* In the previous process, there were two main scenarios depending on the timeframe (less than 24 hrs, more than 24 hrs and in case of a lost phone). There won’t be such a distinction anymore, the process will be the same regardless of the timeframe.
* The previous process instructed CS to contact the driver but didn’t specify how. The new one instructs CS to call drivers and then send an outgoing case if the driver doesn’t respond.
* In the previous process, CS should first ask for a description of the object and then for a consent to share their phone number with the driver. In the new process, these two are merged under one step to speed up the resolution.
* In the new process it will be emphasized that CS shouldn’t ask for a detailed description of the object and should proceed to handling the case even if they don’t know the color, shape, brand etc. of the object to again speed up the resolution.
* In the new process, CS will keep the rider updated more, e.g. they will advise whether the driver found the item or not when telling the rider that the driver will contact them.
* Saying that Bolt is not responsible for lost items is no longer a step in the process.
* User verification instructions will be expanded to cover more possible scenarios (e.g. contact from 3rd party).
* I’ve asked T&W team to update the content of the [automated message|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CD/pages/4293001996/Rider+Lost+Item] so the message can ask the user for a description of the object and consent to share their number with the driver so that CS doesn’t need to do it and thus we can resolve the case faster. It’s being discussed with T&W.

The diagram explains how it works.  I will break it down to you in words so that you can get a better understanding of how it all works. 
A ticket comes in the CS department complaining about an event, if it is either significant or sensitive then it is escalated  to the FST team which will handle the case by sending out emails to the rider trying to get as much information as possible. Once they have it all, the FST team escalate the case to the SME if it is a significant event and lets them handle the issue by either writing or calling the driver. If it is a regular event that requires a   block then it will also be escalated to the SME. The account will be blocked during the time of investigation, they send out a message to the driver asking him if anything unusual happen ?
Based on what the driver will say and all the evidence they will gather, they fill out an assessment tool that lets them know what the global action would be in such cases. Whether it requires a temporary block or permanent block, the SME team will then submit the case in a dedicated slack channel called *fr-ops-safety-blocking* to the OPS quality team. We review the case, and only confirm and ask the SME to block drivers if we have solid evidence (eg: picture that prove that it is an impersonation, or when looking at the history of the driver, if two people who do not know each other describe the exact same behaviour.) I will attach two cases that will show you one block driver and one that was unblock following the lack of evidence. The driver then gets a message from the SME telling them the conclusion of our investigation. We can set up a call tomorrow if you think that it might be clearer to discuss it out loud.

Thanks for flagging. Your above approach is fine. Please note my advice here for ease of deployment/future reference. 

*Advice*

Any form of blocking Drivers on Bolt’s platform carries employment reclassification risks given it interferes with a Drivers ability to do business on their own account as Independent Contractors and evidences a level of control by Bolt. However, as you’ve rightly pointed we can rely on our Fraud Policy to defend Bolt’s position on blocking Drivers when we suspect it's a fraudulent trip to the detriment of passengers.

The process you’ve suggested above puts Drivers on notice their conduct is unacceptable with information on how to correct this prior to their blocking, therefore in my view this is the most pragmatic approach the business can take to mitigate against complaints from regulators and has less of a reclassification risk given Bolt has a commercial right to prevent Fraud on its platform. 

I would, however, recommend changing the language of ‘block’ too ‘suspension’ to be in line with our Fraud Policy. This should be reflected on the back end so that the Driver can still access their invoices on the day their account is suspended but they just cant take rides. Use of the word ‘block’ should generally be avoided where possible to avoid miscommunication with Drivers that may be potential claimants. 

I’ll close this ticket now, reach out if you need anything further.

Many thanks, 

Clarissa

Hey [~accountid:625fb4921046bb0071ddf448],

In a partner integration with Miles, where Miles vehicles are rented to our users, Miles has a significant interest in listed customer data. 

This has the following background:
In Germany, strict liability applies to the vehicle owner (in this case Miles) according to § 7 StVG. This means that a car poses such a danger that the person who lets the vehicle on the road is always liable. In legal proceedings, the claim is therefore always addressed to the vehicle owner; the vehicle driver is only a further debtor against the injured party in addition to the insurance company, against whom a claim can be made.

Damages incurred by Miles as the vehicle owner because the vehicle driver (Bolt User) did not drive well can be recovered by Miles from the vehicle driver. In order to make a recourse claim against this driver (Bolt User), Miles needs the customer data. However, Miles needs the customer data to defend itself in a possible lawsuit and to ask the customer about the accident.


Exculpation from this liability is possible if it is driving without authorisation, which is explained in more detail below. In any case, it is very typical that Miles wants this data and has a legitimate interest in it.

§ 7 StVG reads:
*_§ 7 Liability of the owner, driving without authorisation_*
_(1) If a person is killed, the body or health of a person is injured or an object is damaged while operating a motor vehicle, the owner is obliged to compensate the injured person for the resulting damage._
_(2) The obligation to compensate is excluded if the accident is caused by force majeure._
_(3) If someone uses the motor vehicle without the knowledge and will of the vehicle owner, he or she is obliged to compensate the damage instead of the owner; in addition, the owner remains obliged to compensate the damage if the use of the motor vehicle was made possible through his or her fault. Sentence 1 does not apply if the user is employed by the vehicle owner for the operation of the motor vehicle or if the motor vehicle has been left to him by the owner._

Bolt as a licensed operator is required through its regulatory function to ensure that drivers are in compliance with appropriate signage conditions which may have reciprocal obligations in their driver conditions which they have to comply with as well.

1) Conducting spot checks for compliance of signage conditions = low

2) Suspension for breach of signage conditions = low, unless the driver complies with the breach immediate and limited future breaches are detected.

By default all the predicate pointed in documenation are enabled during the cluster restart:
[https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/cloud-on-k8s/current/k8s-orchestration.html#k8s-advanced-upgrade-control|https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/cloud-on-k8s/current/k8s-orchestration.html#k8s-advanced-upgrade-control|smart-link] 
Those can be only disabled but only in case, when the upgrade of the cluster can be done because of some index issues.

Below you can find example of working predicate during the upgrade.

{noformat}        Message:    Cannot restart node because of failed predicate
        Name:       logs-es-data-warm-v1-a-9
        Predicate:  if_yellow_only_restart_upgrading_nodes_with_unassigned_replicas
        Status:     PENDING{noformat}



From my observation it seems that there is different predicate used when cluster is upgraded (some setting change, version bump, etc) or it is restarted by k8s control-plane. I can say that upgrade predictions like {{if_yellow_only_restart_upgrading_nodes_with_unassigned_replicas}} are more safe for cluster.

* *How will the access point for OneModel's personnel be secured/protected? Please describe the security controls in place.* 
** The access points for One Model personnel are fully managed via InTune, with end users having no admin permissions. These devices also have Windows Defender for Endpoint installed, as well as Zscaler ZIA and ZPA. Zscaler is One Model's DLP solution which prevents regulated data from leaving the endpoints via network (this also includes network printers) or physical (USB) interfaces.
* *How has OneModel implemented more granular access restrictions for other customers that enable OneModel engineers to limit access to what they need, when they need? There is a general concern about access being unlimited and unrestricted to those authorised personnel, as if one of those access points were to become compromised, ALL Bolt data would be accessible to an authorised third party. I recall Stephen mentioning AWS Workspaces — can these potential solutions be explained clearly to Gadir and his team so that a decision can be made and signed-off internally as to whether to adopt these additional controls, or not?* 
** To add to what Stephen provided in his email response on July 27th about AWS Workspaces, One Model Database Engineers are restricted from accessing Redshift Database Clusters from any location other than One Model managed AWS workspaces. This is controlled via AWS security groups / IP allow listing.
* *On the logs, can you confirm that they would reflect exactly what data has been accessed by whom and what was done with it?* 
** Usage statistics (that will be available/accessible on the front end) will provide details on what content, query, and storyboards (as well as what data fields) were viewed by users and when.  In addition, they will also track any data/queries that have been exported out of the tool. 

Thank you.

{code:sql}WITH stats AS (
WITH inputs AS (
SELECT 
d.id AS calculation_id,
d.meta.order_id AS order_id,
d.meta.user_id AS user_id,
d.meta.city_id AS city_id,
json_extract_scalar(d.input, '$.user.creation_ip') AS creation_ip
FROM archive_analytical.user_order_request AS d
WHERE 
d.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -1, current_date) as date)
AND d.created_hour >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -1, current_date) as date)
GROUP BY 1,2,3,4,5
)
SELECT 
i.creation_ip AS creation_ip, 
COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN etl.order_state = 'cancelled' AND etl.user_price > 0 THEN etl.order_id END) AS count_cancellation_fee_rides,
COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN (etl.is_payment_problem OR etl.is_chargeback OR etl.is_final_failed_payment) THEN etl.order_id END) AS count_bad_payment_rides,
COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN etl.order_try_state = 'finished' THEN etl.order_id END) AS count_finished_rides
FROM ng_public.etl_denormalized_commerce_orders AS etl
LEFT JOIN inputs AS i ON i.calculation_id = etl.fraud_calculation_id
WHERE 
etl.order_type = 'rides'
AND etl.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -1, current_date) as date)
GROUP BY 1
HAVING 
(
COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN etl.order_state = 'cancelled' AND etl.user_price > 0 THEN etl.order_id END) > 1 
OR 
COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN etl.order_try_state = 'finished' THEN etl.order_id END) > 1
)
)
SELECT u.user_creation_ip AS KEY, 
COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN u.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -7, current_date) as date) THEN u.user_id END) AS week_users_created, 
COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN u.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -1, current_date) as date) THEN u.user_id END) AS month_users_created,
s.count_cancellation_fee_rides AS month_count_cancellation_fee_rides,
s.count_bad_payment_rides AS month_count_bad_payment_rides,
s.count_finished_rides AS month_count_finished_rides
FROM ng_pii.fraud_user AS u
JOIN stats AS s ON u.user_creation_ip = s.creation_ip
WHERE 
u.created_date >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -1, current_date) as date)
AND u.user_creation_ip IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1,4,5,6
HAVING 
(
(
COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN u.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('day', -7, current_date) as date) THEN u.user_id END) > 7
OR
COUNT (DISTINCT CASE WHEN u.created >= CAST(DATE_ADD('month', -1, current_date) as date) THEN u.user_id END) > 10
)
AND

    		on c.id = a.support_case_id
    where a.created_date >= date('2023-07-01')
	   and a.created_date <= date ('2023-08-09')
        and a.event_type = 'linked'
),
child_cases as ( -- data on created cases
	select 
		g.id  -- child_case_id (which was created by an agent and linked to the original_case)
		, g.user_persona
		, g."source"
		, g.created
		, g.created_date
		, g.state
		, g.tier
		, g.order_id
		, k.issue_key
	from ng_customer_support.etl_data_api_support_case 	  		as g
	left join ng_customer_support.etl_data_api_support_case_issue  	as k
    		on g.id = k.support_case_id
	where 1=1
		and g."source" = 'beehive_outgoing'
		and g.user_persona in ('eater', 'provider', 'courier', 'market_consumer', 'couerier_lead')
		and g.created_date >= date('2023-07-01')
		and g.created_date <= date('2023-07-31')
		and g.state in ('closed', 'solved')
)
select
	cc.user_persona											    as created_case_user_persona
    , cc.id 													    as created_case_id
    , cc.issue_key												    as created_case_issue_key
    , cc_issues.issue_title 										    as created_case_issue_title
    , cc.tier 													    as created_case_tier
    , case when trait.id is not null then 'yes' else 'no' end 			    as is_bolt_market
    , case
	    when oc.support_case_id is null then 'not_linked'
	    else 'linked' end
	    														    as is_linked
    , oc.user_persona 											    as original_case_user_persona
    , oc.support_case_id 										    as original_case_id
    , oc.issue_key												    as original_case_issue_key
    , oc_issues.issue_title 										    as original_case_issue_title
from child_cases						 				as cc
left join original_cases 								as oc
	on oc.child_case_id = cc.id
	and oc.original_case_created <= cc.created
left join ng_customer_support.support_issue_store_support_issue 	as cc_issues
	on cc.issue_key = cc_issues.issue_key
	and cc_issues.is_internal = false
left join ng_customer_support.support_issue_store_support_issue 	as oc_issues
	on oc.issue_key = oc_issues.issue_key
	and oc_issues.is_internal = false
left join ng_delivery.delivery_order_order 					as delivery
  	on cc.order_id = delivery.id
left join ng_delivery.delivery_provider_provider_trait 		as trait
	on delivery.provider_id = trait.provider_id
	and trait.trait_id = 145
where 1=1{code}

A couple of notes:

* I created only external tables, which means that databricks does not manage this data. If it weren’t an external table, deleting the table would also remove the data
* It’s not possible to create tables via REST API, you need to run a {{CREATE (EXTERNAL) TABLE}} statement
* Upon creating a table in unity catalog, databricks reads the data at the given location and checks if the provided schema (columns + types + partitions) matches the actual schema
* Some tables had an empty “comment” as their metadata. Glue does not return this information. So when the create table statement failed, I ran a regular expression to find out which columns had this empty comment and updated the create table statement, and ran it one more time
* The table `analytics_staging.{{etl_business_company_daily_orders}}` has some upper case column names, however, Glue returns all column names as lower cases, therefore I ignored this table, as this was the only table with this problem in the {{analytics_staging_spark}} database.
* In order to avoid re-creating the table every time we sync Glue to Unity, I used Glue’s table update time and stored it as a version property in the Unity schema.
* It seems that there are quite a lot of inconsistencies between the “presto” schemas and “spark” schemas (I mean the {{_spark}} schemas). Sometimes the schema of the table does not match (especially {{_spark}} schemas miss quite often columns and don’t contain partitioning information), and some tables are missing in one schema which contains the other schema, and vice versa.
