Hi [~accountid:5b7bea09d08e47445d6fd01e] , please see below a short summary update:

* The *regulatory framework* would appear to be the following for this new category:
** _In relation to tuk tuk operators:_ [DL 108/2009|https://diariodarepublica.pt/dr/legislacao-consolidada/decreto-lei/2009-66384284] applies as regards the licensing and operating requirements for these vehicles (those were integrated in the draft t&c);
** _In relation to Bolt as an electronic platform:_ it seems that there is a loophole in the law. That is, the combination of the tuk tuk regime with the TVDE regime added to the exception provided for in Article 4(2)(e) of [DL 17/2018|https://diariodarepublica.pt/dr/legislacao-consolidada/decreto-lei/2018-114832295] seems to allow for the onboarding of tuk tuks under the “mere intermediation in the sale or reservation of one-off travel services requested by the customer” exception.
*** Safest legal recommendation: ensure that tuk-tuks made available via the platform comply with all TVDE requirements.
*** Less safer recommendation: maximize the “mere intermediation” exception provided for in Article 4(2)(e) of DL 17/2018, which dispenses a travel agency license and simply adds one service to the menu of services made available by Bolt via its platform. +_RISK: authorities may argue that what Bolt provides is not a “one-off” travel service request and Bolt may be required to obtain a travel operator license._+

* In a decision to move ahead with the less safer recommendation, there are *minimization measures that are recommended by DLA* to ensure Bolt is legally more secure than simply navigating a legal loophole. See those below:
** Fit & proper requirements of both the TVDE operator and the driver;
** Additional requirements for drivers (number of years of driving license, training, contract)
** Obligation to provide vehicles for limited mobility passengers;
** Limited set of reasons to refuse a service;
** Maximum age of vehicles
** Periodic inspection of vehicles
** Minimal value for insurance compensations
** Maximum number of work hours for TVDE drivers and obligation by platforms to set up supervision mechanisms
** Information obligations by platforms (price and calculation formula, digital maps, quality rating mechanisms, vehicle and driver photos, vehicle data, terms for electronic invoice).
*** +_My concern with these measures is that many of those then raise reclassification concerns. WDYT? Could Ops provide already a list of the documentation for onboarding of fleets and drivers; and could it be possible to consider some vehicle and insurance related measures?_+

* The *draft t&c (EN/PT)* are available in the following document: [https://docs.google.com/document/d/1cYFleyfn1ZWpFrwRZFzQ3HZWNnTxFbS_/edit|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1cYFleyfn1ZWpFrwRZFzQ3HZWNnTxFbS_/edit|smart-link] 
* Additionally, just wanted to add a reminder that the driver guidelines should follow the requirements of the Tourism Entertainment Law in relation to information to be provided the client before he sends the request for a tour: (i) specific characteristics of the activities to be carried out, difficulties and possible inherent risks, (ii) material specific characteristics of the activities to be carried out, difficulties and possible inherent risks, (iii) material necessary when not provided by the company, (iv) minimum and maximum age allowed, (v) services offered and (vi) their prices. This would need to be clear to the rider in the app before the person makes a request.

Please let me have your questions and thoughts on the above and draft. Thank you!

For driver feedback, we are looking to set up a process for agents to educate the drivers *manually*. It is crucial we only issue education or suspensions in cases where we are absolutely confident the fault is with the driver, and the issue couldn’t have been caused by road blocks or similar.

Metered price recalculation has been discussed with Fraud team [here|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/GKRJ21X7Z/p1690361425560839], although for a different pattern - passengers leaving vehicles early leading to an overcharge, and eventual full refunds. However, for the same reason as above, it would be crucial for us to make sure we address only the cases where we are confident a behaviour issue is present, and are able to catch all case types:

* Driver ending the trip considerably further than the requested destination (definitely the majority, some examples - [458713436|https://britain-admin.bolt.eu/order/Orders/order/458713436/678114754], [458785696|https://britain-admin.bolt.eu/order/Orders/order/458785696/678418157], [458717457|https://britain-admin.bolt.eu/order/Orders/order/458717457/678133035], [458586414|https://britain-admin.bolt.eu/order/Orders/order/458586414/677606107], [460732819|https://britain-admin.bolt.eu/order/Orders/order/460732819/686856882]
* Cases where the driver goes away from the desired destination, adds mileage, and then returns to the desired destination (example [461054931|https://britain-admin.bolt.eu/order/Orders/order/461054931/688205963])
* Cases when the driver ends the trip slightly away from the desired pick-up to cross a polygon twice. Most commonly airport trips to get a doubled airport fee - [458748318|https://britain-admin.bolt.eu/order/Orders/order/458748318/678280429], [461612455|https://britain-admin.bolt.eu/order/Orders/order/461612455/690508039].

We are seeing similar issues related to unfair wait time fees and cancellation fees, although with a smaller monetary impact.  As we must refund such cases with Rider as actor, there are no factors stopping the drivers from abusing similar issues, I believe that the introduction of manual blocking structure, per the original process, could help reduce related issues.

*Overview:* 

Workday enhances the Request framework and enables you to better track and report on requests by assigning IDs to requests. You also have the ability to create your own ID generator, which Workday uses to create a sequential Request ID.



*3 Sub Points:*

# Workday has updated all versions of the Request REST API to support request IDs and generate a request ID for every new request created using REST. This update applies to these endpoints:

* GET/types
* GET/requests
* POST/request/requests/close
* POST/request/requests/create

2. We deliver a new Request ID report field (secured to the Public Reporting Items domain) on the Request business object so that you can view the ID of requests. 

Workday also added a new ID Generator report field (secured to the Set Up: Requests domain) on the Request Type business object that we can use on standard and custom reports to display the sequence generator for a request type.

3. Workday has updated the Create Request Type and Edit Request Type tasks (secured to the Set Up: Requests domain) with a new ID Generator field that we can use to configure sequence generators for specific request types. We can create our own ID generator format using the Create ID Definition / Sequence Generator task, which Workday uses to create sequential request IDs.

Workday also enhances the Edit Tenant Setup - Business Processes task (secured to the Set Up: Tenant Setup - BP and Notifications domain) to allow us to configure a generic sequence generator for requests using the new ID Generator for Requests field. This ID generator is used by Workday if there isn't one configured for the request type.

Note: If neither the request type nor the tenant have an ID generator, the request is not assigned a request ID.

The current wording is this: "_An account statement along with any invoice shall be made available to the Customer."_. # Customer has amended the background statements at the beginning of the Agreement: “_In case of conflict with_ *_the General Terms and Conditions_* *-_any other parts of the Agreement_-* _these Special Terms shall prevail_“. fyi - the ride-hailing industry in Romania is regulated by primary and secondary legislation, which gives the possibility to the authorities to ask for data from the platforms. And for this reason we need your help 🙂 , because we do not know how to respond to these requests:

* Emergency Ordinance no. 49/2019 regarding alternative transport activities with passenger car and driver
Decision no. 572/2020 for the approval of the Rules regarding the procedure for granting/withdrawing the technical approval for digital platforms for alternative transport with passenger car and driver

According to Art. 26 of Emergency Ordinance 49/2019:
_At the request of the authorities with powers in the field, provided by this emergency ordinance, the operator of the digital platform or the branch of the non-resident operator of the digital platform, as the case may be, will make available to them all the required information that it holds in relation to the performance of the activity by the operators of alternative transport through the digital platform. The provision of this information is carried out in accordance with the legal provisions in force._ 

Emergency Ordinance 49/2019 provides that Police can control only the drivers on the roads, via traffic policemen….

But, according to Art. 11 of Decision no. 572/2020, in order to get the autorisation, Bolt must _prove the representation mandate of the subsidiary ratified by the operator of the digital platform, in which all the rights and obligations conferred on it are mentioned; the right/obligation to make available to public institutions, in accordance with their competences, the data relating to journey, route, passengers, drivers, transport operators, car, location, contracts must be expressly specified._ 

So are the above sufficient for the Police to request this data, or should they also mention articles from Penal Code? 

From what I see in the above request, they only mention the no of the criminal case that Police is investigating, without any details of case and articles from the penal code, which I assume that they should provide.

But just so you know that they might also expect us to comply based on the ride-hailing legislation. Thanks a lot!

The controller itself, not the DPO, is responsible for conducting the DPIA and the DPO has no decision-making power. Recommendations have been made by the DPO team and the controller has addressed the advice and comments, made adjustments or opposed the recommendation, citing reasons. The GDPR does not stipulate an obligation for the controller to follow the advice of the DPO. Thus, the controller complied with the obligation to involve the DPO in the implementation of the DPIA.

+*Short-term solutions*+ in order to tackle this issue could be the following:

* Consult the pricing team who is responsible for the auto closure of these ride did not happen requests. They might have the possibility to push all of these to manual price review where the local agents can check each case and close these according to the situation. This, however, will result in manual work for the agents on price reviews (approx the extra 200 per 30 days so around 7 per day).
* Another option is to tackle these drivers manually in bulk once and then keep monitoring from time to time. But please do keep in mind that this option also requires repetitive assistance and manual work which the fraud team has very limited time and resource availability in general.

1- How do payouts work?

Your payments are calculated automatically every week. A payment cycle runs from Monday (00:00) to the following Sunday (23:59). If your balance is at least 20 GEL, the amount will be transferred from our side to your driver's bank account. Depending on the local bank’s processing time, it may take 1-2 business days for the transaction to be completed and the payout to be received.

We will send your payout to the bank account or mobile wallet linked to your driver profile. 

To see your balance and payout amount, go to the _Earnings_ view from the main tab in the app.



2- What is irregular activity?

By eliminating irregular activity, Bolt provides a safe and convenient platform for drivers and riders. However, in very rare cases, drivers and riders engage in irregular activity.

If the driver engages in an irregular activity, it may lead to an investigation by law enforcement, removal of some trip fares, and temporary or permanent suspension from the platform.
